The Netherlands · Amsterdam

Sep 10 – 13 · 3 nights · Residence Flower Market, on the canal ring

1
Thursday · September 10
Arrival · Koopavond Shopping · Sunset Wine Cruise
Amsterdam
07:15

🛬 Land at Schiphol 📍

Immigration and the EES biometric scan, then bags. Nothing is timed until 20:00, so move at your own pace.

08:45

🚆 Train to Amsterdam Centraal 🧭 Route

15 minutes, every few minutes. Tap a contactless card at the gates (OVpay, ~EUR 4.90) and tap out at Centraal. Then tram 2 or 12 to Koningsplein📍 and 2 minutes on foot. Drop bags at reception.

10:30

☕ First coffee + the Bloemenmarkt 📍

The floating flower market is at your doorstep. Coffee at Crema📍 or Cafeciti📍. Just coffee, lunch is at noon.

12:00

🍟 Lunch at Fabel Friet 📍

The TikTok fries on Runstraat, 6 minutes away, parmesan and truffle mayo. One large to share between the three of you is the right amount, the portions are generous and there is more eating ahead.

13:30

🚿 Check in, shower, change. No nap.

You slept on the overnight leg, and westward travel is the easy direction: you adapt by staying up until a normal local bedtime, not by sleeping now. A shower will do more than a bed will.

If nobody slept a minute on the plane: 30 minutes maximum, alarm on, before 15:00. Anything longer and you will be wide awake at 3am and wrecked for Friday.
14:30

🐟 Daylight, and your first herring 📍

Your body clock thinks it is late evening now, so push through it outdoors: sunlight is what resets you. Walk the Singel📍 bridges to Frens Haringhandel at Koningsplein, 3 minutes from your door the stand locals rate. A broodje haring is about EUR 4, eaten standing up in five minutes. Say "met uitjes en augurk" for onions and pickle, or order kibbeling if raw fish is not for everyone.

Closes around 17:00, so it has to be now. September is past the June new-catch peak but the herring is still excellent.
16:00

🛍️ Nine Streets koopavond 📍

Thursday is Amsterdam's koopavond, the one night boutiques stay open to about 21:00, so do all your souvenir shopping tonight: Friday is a small-bag day and Saturday you are at the beach.

🍪 One sweet stop, pick a side. Van Stapele📍 for the warm chocolate cookie, 3 minutes away, or Winkel 43📍 for the famous appeltaart, 15 minutes north. Not both, dinner is wine and cheese at 20:00.
19:20

🚶 Walk to the pier at Prins Hendrikkade 25 🧭 Walk

It is right by Centraal, about 20 minutes on foot from the Nine Streets, so leave by 19:20. Check in by 19:45 inside the Lovers Café at the mooring, not on the boat.

20:00

🍷 Wine & Cheese Cruise · 90 minutes · this is dinner

Sunset is around 20:10, so you push off in golden light and come back along lit canals. Wine and cheese boards from a seat, on the day your legs have nothing left. Booked and paid, EUR 96, order LOV-R14963017.

This replaces dinner, so book no restaurant tonight. If cheese is not enough after the flight, grab something small on the walk back, you are 10 minutes from the hotel.
21:30

😴 Straight to bed

Tomorrow is the long one and it ends at Anne Frank.

2
Friday · September 11
Van Gogh · Albert Cuyp · Heineken · Anne Frank at Night
Amsterdam

🕯️ Anne Frank is a late slot, so dinner comes first

Entry window is 19:30 to 19:45, out around 20:45. So dinner comes first: Moeders at 17:30, table held to 19:30, then a 7 minute walk.

Walking day, no trams: south to the museum quarter, north again for dinner, about 7 km.

Small bags only. Van Gogh bans backpacks, Anne Frank allows nothing over A4, and you never pass the hotel between them.

09:00

🍳 Brunch at Eggs Benaddicted 📍

Prinsengracht 474, a short walk from the hotel and already pointing south. 4.8 on Tripadvisor. No reservations taken, they seat walk-ins, so arrive at 09:00 rather than 10:00. PLUK📍 in the Nine Streets is the pastel-pretty alternative if the queue is shorter.

10:15

🚶 Walk south through the canal ring 🧭 Walk

25 minutes on foot to Museumplein through the prettiest part of the canal belt: Leidsegracht📍. Leave by 10:45 at the latest.

11:15

🎨 Van Gogh Museum 📍

You walked here through the canal ring, so you arrive at Museumplein📍 with time to spare 🧭 Route. Your booked 11:15 slot. The museum takes 1.5 to 2 hours, his life laid out in order, sunflowers and all. Soft alarm for 13:00. Klook ref GWJ217089. No backpacks, nothing over 45×25×25 cm. The collection is arranged chronologically, so if time runs short the later rooms are the ones to speed through.

13:15

🍯 Graze the Albert Cuyp Markt 📍

The market sits between the Van Gogh and the Heineken, so you eat your way across it on the walk. Share, do not order three of everything: one stroopwafel from Rudi's📍 and one Pat's Poffertjes📍 between the three of you. This is a tasting stop, not lunch: two beers and a full Dutch dinner are still coming.

14:30

🍺 Heineken Experience 📍 · Tour + Rooftop

Ten minutes on foot from Albert Cuyp 🧭 Walk. Book the Tour + Rooftop, EUR 29.95: Your booked 14:30 slot, Klook ref XAV520037. The tour is 1.5 hours self-guided, so you are out by about 16:00, with one drink included on the tour and one on the rooftop. The rooftop is the part non-ticket holders never see. Bring ID, 18+ is enforced.

16:15

🚶 Walk north to the Jordaan 🧭 Walk 🧭 Walk

About 30 minutes along Weteringschans and the Leidsegracht, a canal walk. Do not detour to the hotel, it costs 40 minutes. Tram 7 or 10 if legs are done.

16:45

☕ The buffer: sit down in the Jordaan

Forty minutes doing nothing, five minutes from the restaurant. Anne Frank at 19:30 cannot move, so the slack lives here: if anything overran, you spend this instead of your evening. Make it coffee, not another beer, you have had two and dinner is next.

17:30

🍽️ Early dinner at Moeders 📍

Booked and prepaid, 3 people, EUR 30 off the bill. Rozengracht 251 H, phone +31 20 626 7957. The table is held to 19:30, so eat unhurried, leave at 19:15, walk 7 minutes, enter the museum at 19:30.

🚨 Reconfirm by email before 16:00 on the day, or the reservation is void. They send the message that morning. Do it at breakfast, not later: at 16:00 you are walking out of the Heineken.
Order light, portions are enormous. Two Hollandse Rijsttafel (EUR 24 each, every Dutch classic on one platter) shared across the three of you, plus one erwtensoep, is plenty. Skip dessert. Bring a printed photo of your mum if you remember, they hang it on the wall. If you run late, the table is only held 20 minutes, so email them.
19:30

🕯️ Anne Frank House 📍

Booked, three adult tickets, entry window 19:30 to 19:45. Seven minutes on foot from Moeders 🧭 Walk. About an hour inside, so out around 20:45. Show the QR on your phones, no printing needed. The late slot is the quietest and most contemplative of the day. Book the plain museum ticket, EUR 16.50: the audio tour is included, and the extra EUR 7 introductory program is a 30 minute talk you do not need at this hour. Bags larger than A4 are not allowed, so leave everything at the hotel.

Walk home along the canals afterwards rather than taking a tram. It is the right way to end this particular evening.
🍽️ Breakfast · Lunch · Dinner
Brunch
Eggs Benaddicted📍 then Winkel 43📍 appeltaart mid-morning.
Lunch
Albert Cuyp Markt📍: stroopwafel from Rudi's or Hans Egstorf, plus Pat's Poffertjes.
Dinner
Moeders📍 at 18:00, booked, before the museum.

3
Saturday · September 12
Egmond aan Zee Beach Morning + Leni's House 🏖️🏡
Leni's
08:00

🌷 Early start, flowers in hand

The Bloemenmarkt stalls open around 09:00, so grab Leni's bouquet Friday before closing from the stall beside your hotel and keep it in water overnight. Out the door by 08:30 with the pasalubong.

08:30

🚆 Head north to meet Leni 🧭 Route

Coordinate with her: either she scoops you up, or take the train from Centraal toward Alkmaar / Castricum (~35–40 min, tap in with contactless) and she grabs you at the station. Egmond aan Zee📍 has no train of its own, it is a short drive or Bus 165 from Alkmaar.

10:00

🏖️ Egmond aan Zee, the whole morning 📍

Wide golden sand, rolling dunes, and the J.C.J. van Speijk lighthouse📍 standing over the village, exactly the postcard you saw. September morning light on this beach is glorious. Sea is a brave ~17°C, so barefoot walks, dune photos, and lighthouse-to-water strolls are the program.

11:30

☕ Strandpaviljoen brunch on the sand

Beach pavilion cafés sit right on the sand along the boulevard: coffee, bitterballen, toasties, waves in front of you. Leni will know the good one.

14:00

🏡 Back to Leni's house

The afternoon and evening belong to the house: food, stories, laughter, zero itinerary. This doubles as the farewell-to-Amsterdam dinner in the best possible venue.

21:30

🎒 Back at the hotel, light repack

Checkout is tomorrow morning and Belgium awaits. Ten minutes tonight saves a scramble tomorrow.

🍽️ The day's menu
Brunch
Strandpaviljoen on Egmond's sand: bitterballen, toasties, something warm to drink.
Dinner
Whatever Leni is serving, which will beat any restaurant on this list.
🍴Your Amsterdam food list · what is placed, what is spare
Already in the days
Fabel Friet and Van Stapele Thursday lunch · Crema or Cafeciti Thursday coffee · Zero Zero or Bonburger Thursday dinner · Eggs Benaddicted Friday brunch · Winkel 43 Friday mid-morning · Rudi's or Hans Egstorf stroopwafels and Pat's Poffertjes Friday lunch at Albert Cuyp.
Grab if you pass
Chun📍 · Bunbun📍 · Loop51📍 · Pantopia📍 · Good News📍 · Breadwinner📍 · Layers📍 · Manneken Pis📍 the famous cone by the Dam. Three days only stretches so far, so treat these as opportunistic rather than planned.
Checked open
Verified with 2026 evidence: Eggs Benaddicted (Prinsengracht 474, no reservations), Breadwinner Bagels (two branches), Bonburger (plus a new Noord location), Fabel Friet, Van Stapele, Winkel 43, Frens Haringhandel, Moeders, Foodhallen.
Tap the pin first
Small independents and market stalls I cannot confirm from here: Crema, Cafeciti, Layers, Zero Zero, and the Albert Cuyp stalls (Rudi's, Hans Egstorf, Pat's Poffertjes). Tap the pin the day before for live open or closed status.
Fries verdict
Fabel Friet and Manneken Pis are both excellent and both have queues. Doing both in three days is a lot of fries: pick Fabel Friet, it is 6 minutes from your bed.
Boerejongens ☘️
The red velvet cake is the one you mentioned. Legal for adults here and a well-run place rather than a tourist trap. Thursday only: Friday has Anne Frank at 19:30 and Saturday you are at Leni's. If you go: never buy from anyone on the street, and edibles take up to two hours to land, so a cake eaten before the 20:00 cruise arrives mid-boat. Start far smaller than feels sensible.

Belgium · Antwerp, Brugge & Gent

Sep 13 – 16 · 3 nights · a&o Antwerpen Centraal, beside the station for easy day trips

👥 You are four for the Belgium and Germany legs

Leni travels with you from Antwerp through Cologne, Sep 13 to 19. Book restaurant tables and day-trip train tickets for 4 across Belgium and Germany. She heads home before Interlaken, so everything from Sep 19 onwards is back to 3.

4
Sunday · September 13
Train to Antwerp · Cathedral · Grote Markt
Belgium
09:45

Checkout, then tram to Amsterdam Centraal 🧭 Route

Tram 2 or 12 from Koningsplein, about 12 minutes. Be on the platform by 10:30.

10:45

🚆 Amsterdam Centraal → Antwerpen-Centraal · train 9532, 10:45 🧭 Route

Booked: RNKWVSP, 4 passengers, EUR 33 each. Jenny, Prince John, Lennie and Jan Melchor. About 2 hours, arriving early afternoon.

⚠️ Valid on train 9532 at 10:45 only, not on any Eurostar or other Eurocity service. Show it in the NS International App or printed on plain A4. Bring passports, the ticket is personal and only valid with photo ID. Saver fare: free changes until the day before, EUR 5 to cancel.
Look up as you walk out, the station dome is worth it.
13:00

🎒 Drop bags at a&o, 2 minutes from the platform

Then stroll the Meir📍 shopping street toward the old town, 20 minutes of window-shopping.

16:00

⛪ Cathedral of Our Lady 📍

Belgium's tallest Gothic tower with four Rubens masterpieces inside. It is a Sunday: tourist entry opens 13:00–17:00 (after services), ~EUR 12, so the 16:00 slot works, just do not drift later.

17:15

🏛️ Grote Markt at golden hour 📍

Guild houses, the Brabo fountain, gilded facades. First Belgian beer on a terrace.

🍽️ Sunday dinner: Elfde Gebod

De Arme Duivel is closed Sundays and under renovation, and De Mezzanine closes Sundays and Mondays. Elfde Gebod is open Sunday to Thursday, 12:00 to 23:00, and sits on Torfbrug beside the cathedral, two minutes from where you finish at 17:00.

19:00

🍽️ Dinner at Elfde Gebod Cathedral 📍

Torfbrug 10, in the shadow of the cathedral. A 16th century building filled with saints, angels and pulpits rescued from the Reformation, and Antwerp's oldest and best-rated restaurant. Order the rabbit stew or moules-frites, with a De Koninck or a Trappist. Booked, 19:00, main hall inside. Confirm the party is 4, not 3. Their line is +32 3 288 57 33.

Monday · September 14
Day Trip · Brugge, the Fairytale One
Belgium
1
🚆 Train to Brugge · 09:00 🧭 Route
~1h 25m direct, hourly · buy at the station or SNCB app, no reservation
Standard round trip ~EUR 33 pp, buy in the SNCB app or a machine BEFORE boarding: since July 2026 Belgian trains no longer sell tickets on board and fines run to EUR 500. Trains are never full on a Monday.
2
🏛️ The Markt · 10:45 📍
The postcard square with step-gabled guild houses. Climb the Belfry📍 if the queue is kind: 366 steps, ringing bells, rooftops and canals below.
3
⛴️ Canal boat tour · after lunch 📍
30 minutes · five jetties near the Fish Market · the anchor of the day
Swans, stone bridges, secret gardens from the water.
4
📸 Rozenhoedkaai📍 → Begijnhof📍 → Minnewater📍
The most photographed corner in Belgium, then the quiet beguinage and the swan-filled "Lake of Love".
5
🍫 Chocolate crawl · 16:00
Dumon📍 and The Chocolate Line📍 are the two worth your euros. Buy the box, zero regrets. Trains back run late, dinner in Brugge or Antwerp, your call.
🍽️ Breakfast · Lunch · Dinner
Breakfast
Coffee at Antwerpen-Centraal before boarding.
Lunch
Moules-frites on a Markt terrace, or the brewery lunch at De Halve Maan📍. Then the snack everyone queues for: a warm waffle at Chez Albert📍, the viral Brugge waffle window.
Dinner
De Halve Maan📍 brewery (a Brugse Zot where it is born), or back near the hotel.

Belgium

~50 min, several per hour · then tram 1 to Korenmarkt📍 10 min
2
🖼️ St Bavo's Cathedral · 11:00 📍
The Gent Altarpiece, the Van Eycks' Adoration of the Mystic Lamb. Book the visitor slot online, the AR tour included is genuinely excellent.

Germany · Cologne, Düsseldorf & Bonn

Sep 16 – 19 · 3 nights · Courtyard by Marriott Cologne · 2 rooms

7
Wednesday · September 16
Brussels Afternoon · Evening Train to Cologne
Antwerp → Brussels → Cologne

🖨️ Print the Cologne ticket before you fly

Ticket SVSSVCT is valid only on white A4 paper and may not be shown on a screen. It is non-refundable, non-exchangeable, and valid on the 18:34 train only. Print 4 copies in Manila and keep them flat.

10:00

🎒 Checkout, bags into Antwerpen-Centraal lockers 📍

a&o checkout is 10:00 and strict. The station is next door, so leave the bags there and keep your hands free.

10:30

💎 Last Antwerp hour

Coffee on the Grote Markt📍, a last look at the cathedral, or the Meir📍 for anything unbought.

12:15

🚆 Antwerp → Brussels-Central 🧭 Route

Collect bags, then about 45 minutes. Buy in the SNCB app before boarding, roughly EUR 10 to 12 each. A Belgian ticket to Brussels is valid to any city station, so ride to Central, which puts you five minutes from the Grand Place.

⚠️ No onboard ticket sales in Belgium since July 2026, fines to EUR 500.
13:05

🎒 Bags into lockers at Brussels-Central 📍

Do not drag suitcases round the old town. Lockers are in the station, roughly EUR 5 to 7.

13:30

🏛️ Grand Place 📍

Five minutes downhill from Central and genuinely one of the great squares of Europe: gilded guildhalls on all four sides. Sit down for a late lunch on the square or one street back.

15:00

🚶 The short Brussels loop

All within ten minutes of each other: Manneken Pis📍 (small, silly, obligatory), the glass-roofed Galeries Royales Saint-Hubert📍 for chocolate windows, and Mont des Arts📍 for the view back over the rooftops.

16:30

🧇 Waffle and chocolate, properly

A Brussels waffle from a proper shop rather than a street cart, and chocolate from the Galeries. Last Belgian purchases, Germany is next.

17:40

🚆 Collect bags, hop to Bruxelles-Nord 🧭 Route

Two stops, about 5 minutes, or 25 minutes on foot. Be at Bruxelles-Nord by 18:10 so you find the platform without hurrying.

18:34

🚄 ICE 19 to Köln Hbf, arrives about 20:30 📍

Via Liège-Guillemins and Aachen, roughly 2 hours. Paper tickets and passports out.

The one train on this trip you cannot miss: no refund, no exchange, no later service on this fare.
20:40

⛪ Out of the station into the Dom 📍

The cathedral stands directly outside Köln Hbf, floodlit at night. Two minutes, then walk to the hotel.

21:15

🍺 Late kölsch at Früh am Dom 📍

Two minutes from the cathedral, open late. Small glasses keep arriving until you put your beer mat on top.

Thursday · September 17
Cologne Cathedral · Day Trip to Düsseldorf
Germany
1
⛪ Cologne Cathedral, properly this time 📍 · 09:00
You only saw it floodlit from the station last night. Go inside now: the nave is free, the Gerhard Richter stained-glass window is at the south transept, and the 533-step tower climb is about EUR 8 for the best view over the Rhine. Allow 1.5 hours for both, and go early to beat the coach groups.
🔒 Then five minutes to the Hohenzollern Bridge📍, walk out among the love locks with the cathedral behind you. Düsseldorf can wait until 11:00, it is only 25 minutes away.
2
🚆 Köln → Düsseldorf · 11:00 🧭 Route
25–30 min, several trains per hour, no booking needed · sleep in first
3
🍻 Altstadt, "the longest bar in the world" 📍
300 pubs in half a square kilometer, charming even before noon. Lunch here.
4
🚶 Rhine Promenade · after lunch 📍
Palm-lined, lively, locals everywhere. Walk it south toward the harbor.
5
📸 MedienHafen · 14:30 📍
The warped silver Frank Gehry buildings. Great photos, 25 min walk or a short tram.
6
🍺 One Altbier at Uerige · 16:00 📍
Düsseldorf's dark answer to Kölsch. Friendly rivalry is mandatory. Then train home. Optional on return: Schokoladenmuseum📍 on the river, last entry 17:00 (this is the Cologne chocolate museum, not the Lindt factory you visit in Zurich), only if you are back early.

Switzerland · Interlaken & the Jungfrau

Sep 19 – 22 · 3 nights · Hapimag Resort Interlaken, apartment by the Höhematte

10
Saturday · September 19
Slow Cologne Morning · 9 Hours of Trains · Late Arrival
Cologne → Interlaken

⚠️ Three trains, fixed seats, no cancellation

Ticket 164357590354, 3 people, EUR 256.47. Zugbindung applies: these exact trains only, and the fare cannot be cancelled. In Switzerland it is valid only on the booked service. Carry passports, the ticket needs photo ID.

Your seats: ICE 517 Wagen 6, seats 122–124 · ICE 2559 Wagen 1, seats 32–34 · IC 830 Wagen 5, seats 145–147.

09:00

☕ Unhurried Cologne morning

Nothing before 11:30. Breakfast slowly, repack, and if you want one last look at the Dom📍 it is minutes from the hotel. Checkout by 11:00.

11:30

🚆 Köln Hbf, Gleis 6 📍

ICE 517 departs 11:54. Buy sandwiches and water at the station first, the day is long. Leni says goodbye here.

13:25

🔄 Change at Mannheim, Gleis 5 · 12 minutes

The one tight connection of the day. ICE 2559 leaves at 13:37 from the platform opposite, so be ready with bags before you pull in. If the first train is late, DB rebooks you free on the next service.

13:37

🌄 Mannheim → Zürich, 3h 52m

Recovery Day · Lauterbrunnen · The Captain Ri Pier
Interlaken
09:30

🥐 Long breakfast, then the Coop 📍

Reserved breakfast at Hapimag, then stock the apartment kitchen. Nothing is timed until you feel like leaving.

11:00

🚞 Train to Lauterbrunnen 📍

Twenty minutes from Interlaken Ost, half price with your card. The valley of 72 waterfalls: cliffs a kilometre high, one small village on the floor.

11:30

💧 Staubbach Falls 📍

Twelve minutes on foot from the station. 300 metres of water falling straight off the cliff. Free, and a short path takes you up behind the curtain of spray.

12:45

🍽️ Unhurried lunch in the village

Ninety minutes, no rush. Terraces face the cliffs.

14:30

🚞 Back to Interlaken Ost, then Bus 103

Train 20 minutes, then Bus 103 to Iseltwald, about 25 minutes along Lake Brienz. Both half fare. The lake boat is the prettier alternative if the timetable suits, roughly 45 minutes.

15:40

🎹 Iseltwald, the Captain Ri pier 📍

The lakeside pier where Captain Ri plays piano in Crash Landing on You. CHF 5 turnstile to reach it. Two full hours here: the pier, the tiny village, coffee on a waterfront terrace, and the afternoon light coming down the lake.

17:45

🚌 Bus back to Interlaken

25 minutes. Drop things at the apartment before dinner.

19:00

🫕 Fondue at Bären 📍

Classic cheese fondue in Unterseen. Early night, tomorrow is Jungfraujoch.

🌤️ Check the Jungfraujoch webcams tonight at jungfrau.ch, and reserve the earliest Hapimag breakfast slot at reception.

🌊 If you would rather have Trümmelbach

Trümmelbach Falls📍 is ten glacier waterfalls carved inside the mountain, reached by a lift and wet metal walkways. It is spectacular, but it is also an extra 1h15 visit plus two more bus legs, and it is the slipperiest surface of your trip in road running shoes. Swap it for Iseltwald if you prefer waterfalls to the K-drama pier, but do not try to do both today.

Interlaken

✅ Booked · Klook VXM265051

3 adults, Swiss Half Fare Card holders, PHP 30,960. Interlaken Ost via the Eiger Express route. Includes admission to the Sphinx Observatory, Ice Palace, Plateau and Alpine Sensation, plus a guaranteed seat on the Jungfrau Railway, so no separate reservation needed. Free cancellation with 24 hours notice.

06:45

🥐 Breakfast in the apartment

Hapimag breakfast opens too late for the 08:04 train, so do a Coop run on Sunday: pastries, fruit, yoghurt, coffee. Eat in the kitchen and leave by 07:45. Layers, sunglasses, sunscreen, and the passports are not needed today.

08:04

🚡 Interlaken Ost → Grindelwald Terminal → Eiger Express 📍

Booked, 08:04 up and 14:15 down. ⏰ Be on the platform by 07:54, the ticket says the timing is strict and latecomers may be refused boarding. The earliest slot that still lets you use the Half Fare Card, and about an hour ahead of the coach groups. Train to Grindelwald Terminal, Eiger Express gondola to Eigergletscher, then the cog railway through the mountain. 1h 37m.

📱 Use the Klook app or your phone wallet, not paper. Klook says printed vouchers are not recommended. Each person scans their own QR at the Grindelwald Terminal cable car and again at Eigergletscher, like a ski turnstile. Keep them handy for the return too. On the Interlaken to Grindelwald train you just board; show the QR only if asked.
09:45

🏔️ Sphinx Observatory first 📍

3,571m. Go straight to the viewing terrace on arrival. You are here before the coach groups and before cloud builds, which is the whole reason for the early start. Take the photos first, the Ice Palace and Alpine Sensation can wait. Then the Ice Palace, the Alpine Sensation walk and the Aletsch Glacier view.

Move slowly up here. The air is thin and rushing makes people lightheaded.
13:00

🍽️ Lunch on the mountain

Summit restaurants are fine and expensive. Apartment sandwiches work just as well.

14:30

Different route down: cog railway to Kleine Scheidegg, then through Wengen and Lauterbrunnen. Car-free village, completely different valley views.

17:00

The paragliding meadow two minutes from the apartment. Watch the landings, Eiger and Jungfrau behind. Also a Crash Landing on You spot.

19:00

🍺 Dinner at Hüsi Bierhaus 📍

Craft beer and Älpler macaroni on Postgasse. Pack tonight, Zermatt tomorrow.

Early on purpose: tomorrow is the Matterhorn with a 09:15 start.

Thursday · September 24
Zermatt Rest Day · Sunnegga & Boutiques
Switzerland
1
😴 Sleep in, slow breakfast · 09:00
Apartment or Fuchs bakery on Bahnhofstrasse. Be walking by 10:15, lunch is booked for 12:00 and the path down takes longer than it looks.
2
🚞 Walk to the Sunnegga funicular 📍 · 10:15
Zermatt is car-free, so everything in the village is on foot. The funicular base station sits by the Vispa river at the north end, a flat 10 minute walk from most of the village 🧭 Walk. Show your Half Fare Card, about CHF 13 return.
🚞 10:30 up. Three minutes inside the mountain and you step out at 2,288m. A 10 minute path drops to Leisee📍, the lake with the Matterhorn reflection. Twenty minutes there for photos, leave Leisee by 11:20, then 20 to 25 minutes down to Findeln. You arrive about 11:45 with time to spare.
3
☀️ Lunch at Chez Vrony, Findeln 📍 · booked 12:00 for 3
Booked: 3 seats, 12:00 to 14:00. A 100-year-old family farmhouse at 2,100m with the Matterhorn filling the terrace. Order the Vrony burger or the dried meat and alpine cheese platter. Season runs to Oct 11.
🥾 Getting there: from Leisee, follow the signposted path down to Findeln, roughly 20 minutes downhill on gravel and dirt. No road and no lift to the door, walking is the only way in. 🧭 Walk
⚠️ Decision point: Wednesday Sep 23, 18:00. Cancellation is by email only, until 6pm the evening before. After that a no-show costs CHF 50 per person, CHF 150 for the three of you. You will already be in Zermatt, so check the mountain forecast that evening: if fresh snow or heavy rain is coming, email them and lose nothing. The path is an easy maintained trail in dry weather and a slippery one in ice.
🔙 Getting back, pick one. Walk uphill 25 minutes to Sunnegga and take the funicular down, the easy option. Or walk all the way down to Zermatt, 45 to 60 minutes through larch forest with the village opening up below you, which lands you on Bahnhofstrasse for the afternoon.
4
🛍️ Boutique afternoon on Bahnhofstrasse · 15:00 📍
Watches to window-shop, Läderach📍 chocolate to actually buy.
5
📸 One last Kirchbrücke, then farewell fondue · 17:30
Evening light on the mountain, say goodbye properly. Pack tonight, Lucerne tomorrow.

🧥 What to wear up the mountain

Findeln sits around 2,050m, roughly 450m above Zermatt, so it runs 3 to 4°C colder than the village. Late September means about 8 to 12°C in the shade but 18 to 20°C on a sunny terrace, so layers you can peel off matter more than one warm coat.

Wear: a base layer, a fleece or light knit, and a packable windproof jacket. Running shoes are fine here in dry weather, the path is maintained gravel and dirt rather than a technical trail. If it has rained, take shorter steps and ride the funicular back up from Findeln instead of the long forest descent, which is where mud and wet roots appear. Sunglasses and high SPF, UV is fierce at altitude even when it feels cool. A beanie and thin gloves for the morning funicular.

No dress code to worry about. Hiking clothes are normal there.

Switzerland
1
🍫 Lindt Home of Chocolate, Kilchberg 📍 · 09:30
S-Bahn from Zürich HB to Kilchberg, about 15 min, then a 5 minute walk · half price with your card 🧭 Route
Opens 10:00 daily. The giant chocolate fountain, the café and the largest Lindt shop in the world (over 500 m²) are all free, no ticket needed. Pay only if you want the seven-world museum exhibition, roughly CHF 15 to 19, and book that online in advance, they ask visitors to because demand is high. Allow 1.5 to 2 hours with the museum, or under an hour for the shop and fountain alone.
🎁 This is your pasalubong stop. Factory-shop pricing on the widest Lindt range anywhere, far better value than Bahnhofstrasse. Buy here, then just a few Sprüngli boxes this afternoon. Back at Zürich HB by about 12:30.

👔 Dress smartly, they publish a dress code. No specific table is guaranteed. Running late? +41 44 262 99 00.

🚫Do NOT pre-book these
All Swiss trains
Interlaken→Zermatt, Zermatt→Lucerne, Lucerne→Zürich, the airport run. No reservations exist on Swiss domestic trains. Buy in the SBB app on the day at half fare and sit where you like.
Sunnegga
~CHF 13 return, buy at the valley station on Sep 24. Use the counter, not the turnstile, since your Half Fare Card is digital.
Valley trips
Lauterbrunnen train and the Iseltwald bus, both on Sun Sep 20. Walk-up, half fare, buy in the SBB app at Interlaken Ost.
Why
Swiss fares do not rise as the date approaches, so booking early gains you nothing and locks you into a timetable you may want to change for weather.

What To Order · And What To Drink

Your booked tables and the anchor meals, so nobody stares at a menu in a language they cannot read

🇳🇱Moeders, Amsterdam · Fri Sep 11, 17:30✅ Booked
Order
Two Hollandse Rijsttafel, EUR 24 each, shared across the three of you. It is every Dutch classic on one platter: suddervlees, hachée, stamppot, potatoes, red cabbage, bacon, sausage, gravy. Add one erwtensoep (EUR 9.50), the thick split pea soup with bacon and sausage, to start.
Drink
A Dutch pilsner, Heineken or Amstel, around EUR 4. Or the house red. Skip the jenever tonight, the Dutch gin is lovely but you have a museum at 19:30.
Skip
Dessert. You walk past a dozen better options after 20:45, and portions here are enormous.
🇧🇪Elfde Gebod, Antwerp · Sun Sep 13, 19:00
Order
The rabbit in Trappist beer is the house dish, or moules-frites if mussels are in season, which they are in September. Stoofvlees, the beef stew braised in dark beer, is the other classic. Start with kaaskroketten, deep-fried cheese croquettes.
Drink
De Koninck, Antwerp's own amber ale, served in a rounded glass locals call a bolleke. If you want the serious stuff, a Westmalle Tripel or Chimay Blue, both Trappist, both around 9% so one is plenty. Around EUR 4 to 6.
Note
Belgian beer arrives in its own branded glass. That is not fussiness, the shape is part of it.
🇧🇪De Mezzanine, Antwerp · Tue Sep 15
Order
Stoofvlees met frieten, the beef stew that made De Arme Duivel famous, same kitchen team. Vol-au-vent (chicken and mushroom in puff pastry) is the other signature. Start with garnaalkroketten, grey shrimp croquettes, the best thing Belgium does with seafood.
Drink
De Koninck again, or a Duvel if you want something stronger and golden. Chef Nick's list is short and Belgian.
🇩🇪Früh am Dom, Cologne · Wed Sep 16, 21:15
Order
Late and light after a travel day: Halver Hahn, a rye roll with aged gouda and mustard, despite the name meaning half a chicken. Or Himmel un Ääd, black pudding with mashed potato and apple sauce, which is better than it sounds.
Drink
Kölsch, in 200ml glasses called Stangen, around EUR 2.20 each. The Köbes waiter keeps replacing them without asking and marks your beer mat each time. Put the mat on top of your glass when you have had enough, otherwise they keep coming.
🫕Whymper Stube, Zermatt · Tue Sep 22, 18:00✅ Booked
Order
Fondue moitié-moitié, half Gruyère half Vacherin, the standard and the best. Or raclette if you would rather have melted cheese scraped onto potatoes. One fondue serves two, so two pots for three people.
Drink
Fendant, the dry white from the Valais, is the traditional fondue wine and it is made a valley away from where you are sitting. A Swiss beer works too. Kirsch, cherry schnapps, is the traditional shot alongside.
Tradition
Swiss custom says no cold water with fondue, it is thought to set the cheese. Wine, tea or kirsch instead. Also: whoever drops their bread in the pot buys the next round.
🏔️Chez Vrony, Findeln · Thu Sep 24, 12:00✅ Booked
Order
The Vrony Burger is what people come for, beef from their own farm. The other classic is the platter of air-dried Valais meat and alpine cheese, which is more of a mountain lunch. Rösti with a fried egg if you want something warm.
Drink
A Valais white: Fendant or the more interesting Petite Arvine, both from vineyards you passed on the train up. Their homemade iced tea is famous if you would rather not drink at altitude, and it is the smarter choice before walking back down.
Altitude
2,100m, so alcohol hits harder. One glass here feels like two at sea level, and you still have a path to walk.
🇨🇭Old Swiss House, Lucerne · Fri Sep 25
Order
The Wiener Schnitzel, and nothing else. It is cooked in butter at your table on a trolley, and it is the reason the place is famous. Around CHF 60. Mains here run CHF 51 to 70, so this is a splurge night.
Drink
A Swiss white, or their wine list if you feel like it. This is the evening for one proper glass rather than three cheap ones.
Note
Management changed on 1 August 2026, so older reviews may not match. Worth booking a day or two ahead.
🍜Co Chin Chin, Zurich · Sun Sep 27, 19:00
Order
Slow-cooked ribs and the mixed spring rolls are what reviewers single out. Pho or bun cha if you want something lighter after eight days of cheese and pork.
Drink
Vietnamese beer, or the ca phe sua da, coffee that drips through a filter on your table onto condensed milk. Order it early, it takes a while.
👑Kronenhalle, Zurich · Mon Sep 28, 18:00✅ Booked
Order
Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, sliced veal in cream and white wine with rösti, is the Zurich dish and their best-known plate. Then the chocolate mousse, which arrives as an enormous bowl the waiter spoons from at your table. Do not skip it, it is the thing people remember.
Drink
Their cellar is serious and their bar is a Zurich institution. A glass of Swiss Pinot Noir with the veal, or start with a cocktail in the bar if you arrive early. Budget around CHF 100 each all in.
Dress
Smart. Read their rules of good practice before you pack. It is the one formal evening of the trip.
🍺The rest, in one line each
Bären, Unterseen
Sun Sep 20 · cheese fondue, Fendant or Rugenbräu beer.
Hüsi Bierhaus
Mon Sep 21 · Älplermagronen, alpine macaroni with cheese, potato and apple sauce. Swiss craft beer.
Schäferstube, Zermatt
Wed Sep 23 · lamb, roasted on the open grill. Valais red.
Düsseldorf brauhaus
Thu Sep 17 · Altbier, dark and served the same relentless way as Kölsch. Schweinshaxe or Rheinischer Sauerbraten.
Brugge, De Halve Maan

🛍️Shopping & everything else · plan your own number
Pasalubong
The realistic driver of this line. Swiss chocolate is the classic: a Läderach or Sprüngli box runs CHF 15–30 (~₱1,140–2,280) each, Lindt at a Coop or Migros is a third of that for the same quality. Belgian chocolate at Dumon or The Chocolate Line is EUR 12–25 (~₱820–1,700) a box. If you are bringing home 10 boxes, that alone is ₱10,000–20,000.
Personal shopping
Nine Streets boutiques on your koopavond Thursday, Bahnhofstrasse on the Monday. Entirely up to appetite: ₱5,000 window-shopping, ₱50,000+ if a watch is involved.
Coffee & snacks
Already inside the food budget, but note the Swiss reality: a cappuccino is CHF 4.80 (~₱365) and a pastry CHF 3–5. Three coffees a day for 10 days is ~₱11,000 on its own.
Laundry
20 days needs one wash. Hapimag and Casa delle Stelle are apartments, so a supermarket detergent pod is enough. Hotel service would be CHF 30+ (~₱2,280) a load: budget ₱1,000, or ₱0 if you pack a small bottle.
Restrooms
Not a joke in Europe: EUR 0.50–1 at stations and public toilets across all four countries. ~₱1,500 over 20 days, and always carry coins.
Luggage lockers
Useful on your two 10:00 checkouts with afternoon trains (Antwerp Sep 16, and travel days generally). CHF 6–9 or EUR 4–7 a use: ~₱1,500 across the trip.
Tips
Service is included everywhere on this route. Rounding up is the norm, not 15%: ~₱2,000 total is generous.
Solis data
Your device, shared across three: ~₱3,000–6,000 per person depending on whether you take the monthly unlimited or day passes.
Travel insurance
Schengen requires EUR 30,000 minimum medical cover. For 22 days from Manila: ~₱3,000–6,000 per person.
Cash buffer
Mountain huts, small bakeries and pier turnstiles (Iseltwald's CHF 5) can be cash-only. Carry CHF 100–200 (~₱7,600–15,200) and EUR 100 (~₱6,800), withdrawn from bank ATMs, never airport exchange counters.
Travel tax
₱1,620 each, economy rate. Levied on everyone departing the Philippines regardless of where the ticket was issued. Check your Singapore Airlines receipt first: fares issued in PH often already include it, and you do not want to pay twice. If it is not in there, pay through eTravel, which now requires the travel tax settled before it will generate your QR code. Online payment must be done at least 3 working days before the flight, otherwise it is the TIEZA counter at NAIA on the day.
eTravel
Free, but mandatory. Register within 72 hours before departure (so from Sep 6 for your Sep 9 flight) and again before flying home. Screenshot the QR codes, do not rely on airport WiFi.
Realistic range
₱26,600 lean · ₱46,600 comfortable · ₱81,600+ if serious shopping happens, travel tax included. The cash buffer mostly comes home with you, so it is float rather than spend.

Before You Fly · The Short List

Small things that are easy to forget and annoying to fix from the road

🖨️ Print the Brussels ICE ticket

Ref SVSSVCT. Four copies on white A4, colour or black and white, laser or inkjet, portrait, unchanged font size. It is explicitly not valid on a screen and cannot be refunded or exchanged. Keep them flat, do not fold across the barcode, and check the print is crisp.

📥 Save this guide offline

iPhone: open in Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. Android: Chrome menu, then Add to Home screen. Everyone should do this. All 18 barcodes and every booking reference live inside the file, so it works with no signal at all.

📱 Apps, one per person

SBB Mobile with your own Half Fare Card added, NS International for the Amsterdam train, DB Navigator for the Cologne train, SNCB for the Belgian legs, and the Solis app. Screenshot every QR into one phone album as a backup.

💶 Cash, and where you actually need it

Card works nearly everywhere, but not for the Iseltwald pier turnstile, CHF 5, public toilets across all four countries, some market stalls at Albert Cuyp, and a few coin lockers. Withdraw euros in Amsterdam and francs during the Zürich HB layover on Sep 19. Use bank ATMs, never Euronet, and always decline conversion to pesos.

🧳 Bag rules that catch people out

Van Gogh: no backpacks, nothing over 45×25×25 cm. Anne Frank: nothing larger than A4. You do not pass the hotel between them, so Friday Sep 11 is a small-bag day and any real buying happens on Thursday's koopavond.

👔 One formal evening

Kronenhalle, Mon Sep 28. They publish a dress code, so pack something smart. Every other dinner on the trip is relaxed, including the mountain restaurants where hiking clothes are normal.

🌤️ Two weather decisions

Sun Sep 20 evening: check the Jungfraujoch webcams. Free cancellation with 24 hours notice through Klook, so if Monday looks socked in, move it. Wed Sep 23 evening: buy the Matterhorn ticket only once the forecast looks good. Wed Sep 23, 18:00 is also the free-cancellation deadline for Chez Vrony.

⏰ The times that cannot slip

Sep 10, 19:45 cruise check-in at Prins Hendrikkade 25. Sep 11, 16:00 reconfirm Moeders by email or the table is void, then 19:30 Anne Frank entry. Sep 16, 18:34 ICE 19 from Bruxelles-Nord. Sep 19, 11:54 ICE 517 from Köln. Sep 21, 07:54 on the platform at Interlaken Ost. Sep 29, 08:00 leave for the airport.

Twenty days · four countries · three of you, and Leni for the middle stretch

Have the best time.
